label: D2 after a1 -> S1 (common), when policy not strongly committed to a1
explanation: Fires only at D2 (DELAY_2) and essentially only when the agent chose a1 and reached S1 via the common transition (in_action=1 & in_state=S1: 99.3% recall, 99.8% of mass). Never fires at D1/GO, on a2 choices, or on S2 (rare a1->S2 gets only tiny activations). Within a1->S1c steps it is silent or weak during long stable runs of rewarded a1 when the model is strongly committed to a1 (high choice logit); adding choice < 2.78 raises dev F1 from 0.78 to 0.84 (precision 0.64 -> 0.78). Magnitude is largest when a1 is an unusual choice: a single a1 trial inside a run of a2 choices while S2 is good (top examples), i.e. a surprising/exploratory a1->S1 visit. All variables are observed at D2 (choice is the model own policy logit).

issues: Factual claims check out on dev. Feature is active only at D2 (D1 0/380619, GO 0/380619 steps). It never fires on a2 (in_action 2: 0 active). S2 gets 563 actives holding 0.2% of mass. Base predicate a1->S1 at D2: P 0.644, R 0.993, mass recall 0.998, F1 0.782 (test 0.793). Adding choice<2.78: dev F1 0.842, test P 0.789, R 0.917, F1 0.848, mass recall 0.973. These match the reported numbers.

The 'unusual a1' claim, which the original agent did not measure, holds up. a1->S1 with prev_action==2 has precision 0.991. With good==S2 it has precision 0.868. With good==S1 precision falls to 0.628.

No systematic counterexample class remains. On test, misses are 7302 steps holding 2.7% of mass: weak activations on a1->S1 with choice >= 2.78, plus a few tiny S2R ones. Precision for choice>=2.78 within a1->S1 is only 0.21, and those cases hold 2.4% of mass. The false positives are a1->S1 inside long rewarded a1 runs, where activation is near zero and choice sits just under the threshold. This is graded falloff, not a separate class.

Minor caveat: 'choice' is the policy logit read out at the D2 step itself (the variable list says it is meaningful at GO), not the logit at GO. The 2.78 cutoff is a quantile-bin edge. Cutoffs from 2.0 to 3.5 give similar F1 (0.83 to 0.85; 2.0 gives test F1 0.849), so the exact cutoff does not matter.

Predicates built only on observed history do worse than the choice predicate. Excluding stay & prev_reward & prev_common gives F1 0.61. choice<2.78 & prev_reward==1 gives F1 0.70. value>8.1 gives F1 0.41. So the policy logit is the best available summary of 'not committed to a1'. No future variables are used.
